report.summary: Chunk 2 of 4: helper functions (_bus_path, _turns_of, _chain_head, _quorum_counts, _evidence_paths) and render_markdown. All claims checked and kept.

claims.text: Where the canonical record lives. Explicit field wins; otherwise derived from the council id, which is how bus.py names the file.
claims.why: The function checks explicit fields before falling back to council_id derived path.

claims.text: A transcript may be the turn list itself, or an object/dict carrying one.
claims.why: Function handles None, Mapping (extracts 'turns' etc.), list/tuple directly, and other objects via _field.

claims.text: The chain head digest a reader verifies the bus against. Explicit field wins; otherwise the last turn's entry_sha, which IS the head by construction in an append-only chain.
claims.why: Checks transcript fields first, then verdict fields, then last turn's entry_sha.

claims.text: (answered, requested, answered_vendors, missing_vendors). Counts are derived from the vendor LISTS when present, because a list is checkable against the transcript and a bare integer is not.
claims.why: Returns tuple of four; derives counts from lists when present, falls back to integer fields.

claims.text: Paths named by the evidence, for the path-marker half of the floor.
claims.why: Collects paths from evidence items and verdict's 'paths' field, filtering empty strings.

claims.text: Order is deliberate and load-bearing: outcome and the quorum honesty line lead, so a degraded council is the first thing a reader sees and cannot be skimmed past.
claims.why: Outcome rendered first (line ~330), quorum warning immediately after (lines ~340-350).

claims.text: Then EVERY dissent verbatim with its author -- BEFORE the convergence, because the dissent is the only part that could not have come from asking one model twice.
claims.why: Dissent section (## Dissents) rendered before convergence section (## Where the vendors converged).

claims.text: Then where the vendors converged, evidence digests, per-vendor cost/latency, the deliberation itself, and finally the provenance footer (bus path + chain head) that lets a reader verify all of it offline.
claims.why: Sections appear in order: convergence, evidence, cost/latency, deliberation, then provenance footer (---).

claims.text: Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.
claims.why: No I/O, network, or gate operations in the function body.

claims.text: CONVERGENCE, not 'majority'. A majority is a DECISION; convergence is an OBSERVATION about what the vendors said. The council package carries no approve/reject/score/majority/consensus field on purpose -- absence of the field is the control, not a docstring -- and a rendering that reintroduces the word structurally reintroduces the temptation to read it as a verdict. The legacy aliases are kept only so an older payload still renders.
claims.why: Variable named 'convergence' and uses _field with aliases including 'majority'. Section heading says 'Where the vendors converged' not 'majority'.

claims.text: The advisory banner is UNCONDITIONAL. A verdict arriving without the marker is a contract violation, so we say so instead of quietly rendering it as if it carried authority.
claims.why: Advisory banner always added (line ~335). If advisory is not True, adds a caution note (lines ~337-339).

claims.text: DISSENT LEADS. Not a stylistic choice: the dissent is the only content in this document that could not have been produced by asking one model twice. Convergence among vendors with overlapping training data is cheap; the objection is what four egress paths were actually paid for. Rendering it after -- and therefore below -- the agreement makes the informative half read as a footnote to the uninformative half.
claims.why: Dissent section appears before convergence section.

claims.text: A vendor that did not speak has no content; an empty fence is noise that makes a silent turn look like an empty answer.
claims.why: Conditionally adds text only if text is non-empty (line ~367).

claims.text: A turn that did not SPEAK is the quorum honesty story at turn level: bus.py records 'refused' / 'unavailable' / 'budget_exhausted' / 'anomaly' rather than dropping the vendor, so rendering the status is the difference between 'three vendors agreed' and 'one was never asked'.
claims.why: Checks status and renders note if not 'spoke' (lines ~395-401).

claims.text: Paths an egress lane declined to send are NAMED, not counted -- a vendor reasoning over less evidence than the others is not an equal voice, and hiding that would make the roster look stronger than it was.

observations.what: The advisory banner is always added, but if advisory is not True, a second caution is appended. The banner text says 'ADVISORY ONLY -- this verdict promotes nothing. THE GATE DECIDES, NOT A MODEL.' This is unconditional as stated.
In the evidence table, if an item is a string/bytes, it renders with '(no digest)'. If it is a dict, it extracts label and digest. This matches docstring.
The per-vendor cost/latency table uses _field with multiple aliases. If cost or latency is None, renders 'n/a'.

handoff.purpose: Contains helper functions (_bus_path, _turns_of, _chain_head, _quorum_counts, _evidence_paths) and render_markdown function for rendering council verdicts as markdown.

symbols.name: _bus_path
symbols.note: Determines bus path from verdict/transcript fields or council id.

symbols.name: _chain_head
symbols.note: Gets chain head digest from transcript/verdict fields or last turn's entry_sha.

symbols.name: _quorum_counts
symbols.note: Returns answered/requested counts and vendor lists.

symbols.name: render_markdown
symbols.note: Renders council verdict as markdown string.
